sections.h2: Where is Williston, North Dakota, and what is around it?
sections.html:
Williston is in the northwest corner of North Dakota, at the crossroads of U.S. Highways 2 and 85, near the confluence of the Yellowstone and Missouri rivers at the upper end of Lake Sakakawea. It is 18 miles from the Montana border and 60 miles from the Canadian border.

The city covers about 25.9 square miles. It was founded in 1887 and named for Daniel Willis James, a merchant and capitalist and a friend of railroad magnate James J. Hill. Fort Union and Fort Buford, and the Missouri and Yellowstone confluence west of town, tie the area to the fur trade and the Lewis and Clark era.

sections.h2: How fast did Williston grow, and why does it matter for sellers?
sections.html:
Williston roughly doubled in size over a decade, and that growth explains why its housing stock is so varied. The Census Bureau counted 14,716 residents in 2010 and 29,160 in 2020, and estimates 29,522 for July 1, 2025.

MeasureFigure
Population, April 1, 201014,716
Population, April 1, 202029,160
Population estimate, July 1, 202529,522
Change from 2020 base to July 20251.3 percent
Growth, July 2012 to July 201313.9 percent, fastest of any city its size in the country

A 2014 Census Bureau blog post tied the growth to oil and gas extraction in the Bakken shale formation. It reported that Williston passed 20,000 residents for the first time in 2013 and that Williams County had the fastest housing unit growth in the country among counties with 5,000 or more units, at 15.6 percent in a single year.

Growth since the 2020 estimates base has been 1.3 percent. For a seller, the practical effect is that many Williston homes were built or bought within the same short period, and buyers compare them closely. The figures are on the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Williston.

sections.h2: What is Williston's weather like, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Williston has a cold semi-arid climate that borders on humid continental, and winter dominates the maintenance calendar. The normal January mean temperature is 11.5 degrees Fahrenheit and July averages 70.4.

  • On average there are 39 days a year with a low of 0 degrees or below and 7 days with lows of minus 20 or colder.
  • Snowfall averages 48.2 inches per season, and the record is 107.2 inches in the winter of 2010 to 2011.
  • Precipitation averages 14.88 inches a year, with June and July the wettest months.
  • Extremes run from minus 50 degrees to 110 degrees.

The area has also seen severe weather. A rolling cyclone killed two people in 1907. Inspectors and buyers tend to focus on furnaces, insulation, roofs that hold snow, and any plumbing exposed to freezing. Climate details come from the normals on Wikipedia.

sections.h2: What rules apply to crew housing, campers and temporary dwellings in Williston?
sections.html:
Williston limits the use of campers and other nonpermanent structures as permanent housing, and the rules reach property owners as well as occupants. If you own a lot where workers have been parking RVs, this is the first thing to sort out before you sell.

Under Chapter 5.5 of the city code, a camper vehicle may not be used for permanent habitation in residential, commercial or industrial zones. A violation brings a written warning to the camper's owner or, if the owner cannot be identified, to the owner of the parcel. The ordinance makes violations a class B misdemeanor outside the construction-site guidelines and sets a fine of $500 per day per camper vehicle.

  • Construction sites may use RVs for construction workers, up to 10 units, with a monthly permit that costs $200.
  • RVs must be removed before the city will issue a certificate of occupancy.
  • Residents and visitors may use a camper on developed property for seven days without a permit, and no more than 28 days in a calendar year.

The city's zoning ordinance separately defines temporary workforce housing, and its list of amendments shows moratoria on processing workforce housing applications and on tent structures. Check the code on the city's code site or ask the Planning and Zoning Department how your parcel is classified.

sections.h2: How do mineral rights affect a Williston house sale?
sections.html:
Mineral rights can be separated from the surface by a deed, and North Dakota statute sets default rules for how deeds are read. Under N.D.C.C. 47-10-25, in a surface deed executed on or after July 1, 1983 that reserves any minerals, all minerals of any nature are treated as reserved unless they are specifically excluded by name. Gravel, clay and scoria pass with the surface unless the deed reserves them by name.

Section 47-10-24 sets a default for conveyances of mineral rights, which are read to convey all minerals except those specifically excluded by name. Because the wording matters so much, a seller should find the vesting deed and any earlier reservations before agreeing on a price. A title company or an attorney can confirm what you own. Read both sections in the official Title 47 chapter 10 text.

sections.h2: How is property tax handled in Williston?
sections.html:
Williams County bills and collects property tax for Williston homes, and the state formula applies. The State Tax Commissioner says assessed value is 50 percent of market value, and taxable value for residential property is 4.5 percent of true and full value, which is then multiplied by the total mills of the entities that tax your parcel.

  • Real property tax is due January 1 following the year of assessment and payable without penalty until March 1.
  • A 5 percent discount is allowed for real estate taxes paid in full on or before February 15.
  • Williams County says statements can be paid by mail, in person, by phone at 701-577-4530 or online, and that owners who have not received a statement by December 31 should contact the Treasurer.
  • The county's iTax system lets you search parcel valuations and current tax bills. The Recorder's Office is at 701-577-4540.

Property owners who disagree with a valuation can appeal through the State Tax Commissioner's Property Tax division at 701-328-3127. See the county's property information page.

sections.h2: What permits and flood rules might come up in Williston?
sections.html:
Williston's zoning ordinance requires a permit from the City Building Official before any development in a special flood hazard area. If your property is near water or low ground, ask the city whether it is mapped, and keep the permit history for any improvements.

The ordinance also requires owners in the downtown area to apply to the Design Review Board before applying for a building permit, and it limits accessory buildings and signs by zoning district. Because Williston grew quickly, check that additions, garages and finished basements were permitted. Unpermitted work is easier to resolve before a listing than during an inspection period.

sections.h2: What do I have to disclose, and what are my selling options in Williston?
sections.html:
North Dakota law requires a seller of a residential dwelling with up to four units to give a written disclosure of material facts before the buyer signs final acceptance, under N.D.C.C. 47-10-02.1. Exceptions include foreclosure sales, sales by a fiduciary administering an estate, and certain transfers to family members. Section 47-10-02.2 requires a separate written radon disclosure.

Williston sellers generally choose between a listing, a sale on their own, and a cash purchase by a buyer who takes the house as-is. A cash sale is often worth comparing if the house was used as a rental or crew house, has deferred maintenance, or is an inherited property you do not want to manage. We do not quote prices here, but Cash Home Buyers can review a Williston address and explain how an offer works, and you owe nothing if you decline.

faqs.q: How many people live in Williston, ND?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 29,522 residents as of July 1, 2025. The April 2020 census count was 29,160 and the 2010 count was 14,716.

faqs.q: Why did Williston grow so quickly?
faqs.a: A 2014 Census Bureau analysis tied western North Dakota's growth to oil and gas extraction in the Bakken shale formation. Williston was the fastest-growing city of its size in the country between July 2012 and July 2013, at 13.9 percent.

faqs.q: Can workers live in RVs on my Williston lot?
faqs.a: Only in limited cases. The city's camper ordinance bars permanent habitation in campers in most zones, allows construction-site RVs with a $200 monthly permit, and sets a $500 per day fine per camper for violations. Confirm your parcel's zoning with the city.

faqs.q: Do I keep the minerals when I sell a Williston house?
faqs.a: It depends on the deed. North Dakota statute treats a surface deed that reserves minerals as reserving all minerals unless they are excluded by name, and gravel, clay and scoria pass with the surface unless reserved. Have a title professional read your deed.

faqs.q: When are Williams County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real property tax is due January 1 after the year of assessment and payable without penalty until March 1. Taxes paid in full by February 15 earn a 5 percent discount.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Williston house that has deferred maintenance?
faqs.a: Yes. You still owe the buyer the written disclosure required by North Dakota law, and a buyer that purchases as-is decides whether to take the house in its present condition.
